propositions: The inert-config gate matches field names globally by building a single set of all attribute names read anywhere under src/rebar, so a field is satisfied by any same-named attribute on any unrelated object, producing false negatives when common names like 'enabled' or 'path' are reused across configs.

CodeHealthConfig.enabled had zero read sites but passed the gate because .enabled was read on unrelated configs (UiConfig.enabled, McpConfig.auth_enabled, etc.), while CodeHealthConfig.analyzers was uniquely named and correctly failed the gate, demonstrating the defect is luck-based name collision not a real check.

The fix must resolve each read to its owning dataclass through receiver resolution (section attributes, annotations, assignments, return types, branches, call-site propagation) rather than bare terminal-name membership, so only reads of that class's instance satisfy the field.

Four fields are newly flagged by the corrected gate and are all live: McpConfig.readonly, McpConfig.allow_llm, McpConfig.allow_jira_sync, and JiraConfig.allow_insecure; each receives a factual # read-via: marker naming its actual reader, not a product triage decision.

The fix must be accompanied by accurate # read-via: markers for newly-flagged fields or tracking-ticket pointers for genuinely inert ones, never silent exemptions; existing negative fixtures (ReconcilerConfig.lock_lease_secs, VerifyConfig gate-key fields) must remain passing via their pre-existing markers.

Test migration requires owner-resolution contract changes to both test_check_config_reads.py (adding Config root dataclass and section field) and test_check_config_reads_heldout.py (inverting the same-named attribute collision test to expect firing), plus RED-first proof that the old gate silently passes inert fields with reused names while the fixed gate fires on them.
